decisions.reason: This small-volume ionization chamber remains very close to the firm's core dosimetry, calibration, and clinical-support knowledge, so customer feedback is likely to be absorbed and used for refinement rather than withdrawal, although some overlap risk within the chamber portfolio remains.

This chamber also fits the firm's established detector and service capabilities well, making continued support and incremental improvement more likely than exit, with only modest risk from portfolio rationalisation among similar products.

A standard clinical ionization chamber line sits at the center of the firm's mainstream business, and its broad use, multiple models, and strong calibration infrastructure make discontinuation within a year unlikely.

An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry is a natural extension of the firm's long-standing measurement and QA expertise, so management would expect to keep learning from clinical use and retain it rather than remove it.

A thimble ionization chamber is a classic, highly related product for this firm's knowledge base and accredited calibration capabilities, so it is more likely to be maintained unless replaced by a clear successor product.
